clue.text: American aircraft are first that got ditched

indicators.note: the aircraft word is placed ahead of the American one in the answer

parts.note: a jet is a type of aircraft
Sam, as in Uncle Sam, personifies an American

explanation.surface: US military planes are said to be the first to have been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius makes 'aircraft' singular in the wordplay despite the plural 'are'; JET goes first, then SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship, i.e. goods deliberately jettisoned.

clue.text: Goon upset some members of church assembly

parts.note: Eccles is a character from the Goon Show, the 1950s BBC radio comedy

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top
only some of the word for lay members is used, its last letters dropped

parts.note: the laity are the ordinary lay members of a church

explanation.surface: A clownish figure disrupts part of a church congregation's meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes only part of the laity word and 'upset' turns that part upward. The Goon Show was a famous 1950s British radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek ecclesia was an assembly, and the adjective describes things pertaining to a church gathering.

clue.text: Family undresses with change of heart

indicators.note: the central letters of the word for undresses swap places, altering its heart

parts.note: to undress is to strip, so undresses means strips

explanation.surface: A household takes its clothes off, then has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: In STRIPS the middle pair R and I trade places, giving STIRPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirps is a legal and genealogical term for a line of descent, a branch of a family.

clue.text: Miner fails with endless speculation on what's for afters

indicators.note: a miner who fails comes apart, so his letters are rearranged
the final letter of the speculation word is cut off

parts.note: a guess is a piece of speculation

explanation.surface: A collier who keeps getting it wrong wonders what pudding will be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' makes MERIN from MINER; 'endless' trims GUESS to GUES. 'Afters' is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringues, baked whipped egg white and sugar, are a typical dessert, which Britons call afters.

clue.text: Out of drink — it's going elsewhere

parts.note: ex is a Latin prefix meaning out of or from
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of drink, which has disappeared somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An export is a product shipped out of the country, sent to another place abroad.

clue.text: Greek beak is hard on men with a record

indicators.note: on places the hard letter alongside the men, ahead of them in the answer

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A tough Athenian judge leans on his staff, who have criminal records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate; 'with a record' attaches the record to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephor was one of the five chief magistrates of ancient Sparta, a Greek official with judicial power.

clue.text: Raising hat, I strike an inoffensive type

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a cap is a hat
to fist is to strike with the fist

explanation.surface: Someone doffs their hat and then lands a punch on a harmless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns CAP into PAC at the top of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist refuses to use violence, so is by principle a harmless, non-aggressive sort of person.

clue.text: "Get up, Knight! The Queen!" — and he does

indicators.note: to get something up is to rig or arrange it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch bids a newly dubbed knight to stand, and he obeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' looks like the monarch's command but rearranges SIR plus ER. 'he does' defines the answer: the man who gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is someone who gets up from bed or a kneeling position, as an early riser does.

clue.text: One for a rich tea cracker is more like a hair shirt

indicators.note: a cracker breaks the letters up into a new order
one, the Roman numeral I, takes the place of the letter A

explanation.surface: Someone wants a cheap biscuit to go with their Rich Tea while wearing scratchy penitential clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich Tea is a plain British biscuit. Swapping its A for I leaves RICHTEI, which 'cracker' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair shirt is a coarse garment worn as penance, notably irritating to the skin, so scratchier.

clue.text: Address for a lady in blue?

definitions.text: Address for a lady in blue?

parts.words: Address for a lady in blue?
parts.note: a criminal caught red-handed admits guilt to the arresting officer; a fair lady officer in blue uniform could be addressed this way

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock admission of a caught criminal to a police officer, punning on fair meaning attractive.

clue.text: Reporter's got a point that's cutting

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, and the possessive 's gives the S
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A journalist has a sharp edge to his writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw, a tool used for cutting metal.

clue.text: Where cows yet turn frisky

indicators.note: frisky animals jump around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere livestock still turn and gambol.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is the rural south-west of England, Devon, Cornwall and Somerset, known for dairy farming.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a region, so it serves as a place, answering the question where.

clue.text: New brooms for cleaner hospitals?

parts.note: plays on the saying that a new broom sweeps clean: new managers tidying up hospitals bring in wholesale changes

explanation.definitionFit: Radical overhauls are what an incoming new broom introduces, literally brushing with fresh brushes.

clue.text: Thatcher's frightened of German detail

indicators.note: de-tail means remove the tail, the last letter

parts.note: Fritz is an old slang name for a German

explanation.surface: A former prime minister was scared of the finer points of German.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher famously used the dialect word in the Commons, hence 'Thatcher's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frit is a Midlands dialect word for scared, made famous by Margaret Thatcher.

clue.text: So entertaining a classy character is very fast

indicators.note: entertaining means holding inside, as a host has guests within

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus or so
U means upper-class
a character in a play is a person

explanation.surface: Thus amusing a refined figure is extremely quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' looks like a link word but is the Latin container. U for upper-class is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic means faster than the speed of sound, so exceedingly quick.

clue.text: Sound of two boys squashing Conservative leader

indicators.note: the boys' names and the party word are spoken together to give the answer

parts.note: Eddie and Al, two boys, with Tory, a Conservative, squeezed between them

explanation.surface: Two lads gang up on the head of the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashing' places TORY between EDDIE and AL; said together they give the answer. In Britain a newspaper's leader is its opinion column.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader, or leading article, is a newspaper's opinion piece written by the editor.

clue.text: 16 state spoilt nice scene

indicators.note: a spoilt scene is disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ignorant ruins a pleasant view.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is lack of knowledge, the condition of being unaware or uninformed.

clue.text: I admit being without — no, with — no clue

indicators.note: the admit word is outside, wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: to grant a point is to admit it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they lack something, corrects themselves, and admits they have no idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's self-correction ('without — no, with') is a deliberate joke; only 'being without' does any work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignorant means lacking knowledge, having not the faintest idea about a matter.

clue.text: Pigs soiled wrongly by tittle-tattle

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Dirtied pigs are maligned by chit-chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is trivial talk about others, synonymous with chatter and rumour.

clue.text: Descendant of Abraham returned without a purpose

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed word wraps around the article
returned means the purpose word is sent back, reversed

parts.note: a use is a purpose

explanation.surface: Someone came back having no reason to be there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives ESU, and 'without' (meaning outside) puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau was Abraham's grandson, son of Isaac in Genesis, and so of his line.

clue.text: Smart, but without issue dubious

parts.note: SP, sine prole, is Latin for without offspring, used in genealogies
iffy means doubtful

explanation.surface: Someone is stylish, but having no children makes them suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiffy is informal for stylish and well dressed.

clue.text: Length in additional copy needs reduction

indicators.note: the length word is placed inside the two copies

parts.note: a carbon is a copy, and a print is another copy
a print is a further copy
a foot is a length

explanation.surface: Extra pages in a duplicate need cutting down.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, 'additional copy', supplies two different copies, and the definition is a fresh one: the thing environmentalists say needs cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon footprint is the greenhouse emissions one causes, something environmentalists urge everyone to cut.

clue.text: Branwell, shorter by a head, weakest of the family

indicators.note: the first letter of the surname is cut off

parts.note: Branwell Bronte was the brother of the novelists Charlotte, Emily and Anne

explanation.surface: The only Bronte brother was the family's weak link.
explanation.walkthrough: Branwell, the dissolute Bronte brother, fits the surface, but the answer is a dialect word for a runt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronte is an old dialect form of runt, the smallest and feeblest animal in a litter.

clue.text: This could make a bloomer, say

definitions.text: This could make a bloomer, say

parts.words: This could make a bloomer, say
parts.note: a bloomer is a British crusty loaf, baked from the powder milled from grain; it also sounds like a word for a bloomer in the garden

explanation.definitionFit: Milled grain powder is the basic ingredient of bread, including the long loaf called a bloomer.

clue.text: Trouble after a beer gets to the bird

indicators.note: the trouble word comes after the beer word

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Bother after a drink gets someone to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a young woman, which is the surface; the answer is a real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Pintado is another name for the guineafowl or the pintado petrel, both birds.

clue.text: Dreamed of childhood

definitions.meaning: something dreamed of exists only ..., imagined
the earliest period of a life

explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is early childhood; split into two words it means existing in the imagination.

clue.text: It's preferable to be a speculator

definitions.meaning: something preferable is superior, of more value

explanation.definitionFit: Better means more desirable, and also, read as one who bets, a gambler.

clue.text: Lacking expertise, they are meanly treated

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amateurs are handled stingily.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are non-professionals, people without specialist knowledge of a field.
